reason: The run is already consistent on "shepherd" (with "tending sheep" for the literal, objectless use in Luke 17:7), so this entry is a judgment call, made to lock in a departure and not to repair drift. In Revelation 2:27, 12:5 and 19:15 the run departs from the traditional "rule", and the note at 2:27 justifies the choice by consistency with other chapters the translator cannot see. Competent translators split between "rule", "shepherd", "tend" and "feed" for this verb, so a later run could easily diverge without a fixed decision.
sense: to act as shepherd: literally to tend a flock, and figuratively to lead, care for or govern people as a shepherd does, including the royal and iron-rod uses

alternates.when: Literal herding with no object expressed, where English needs the object supplied, as in Luke 17:7.

traditional: feed or rule in the King James tradition; shepherd or tend in most modern versions, but still rule in the iron-rod verses of Revelation
rationale: The Greek verb is built on the ordinary word for a shepherd and means to do a shepherd's work. A first-century reader heard that image even where the subject is a king or church leader, because shepherd was a standing picture for a ruler in the Greek Old Testament. "Feed" is too narrow and "rule" drops the image, while "shepherd" is still clear English. Using it throughout also lets the reader see that Revelation uses the same verb for the Lamb's care in 7:17 and for the iron rod in 2:27, 12:5 and 19:15.
standard_view: Most modern translations use "shepherd" or "tend" for the pastoral passages (John 21:16, Acts 20:28, 1 Peter 5:2) and "shepherd" in Matthew 2:6 and Revelation 7:17. In Revelation 2:27, 12:5 and 19:15 nearly all have "rule", and standard lexicons list these verses under a sense of ruling with destructive effect. Some scholars argue that there, following the Greek form of Psalm 2:9, the verb is closer to "crush" or "devastate". A minority of literal versions keep "shepherd" in those verses. In Jude 1:12 many versions have "feeding themselves" or "caring only for themselves".
